summary: The security relock reproduces: both lock digests match, only the litellm entry changes, all release hashes match PyPI, the hashed installation passes, and the pinned scanner returns before 1/0 and after 0/0. The remaining defects concern verification scripts that report successful exit codes on failing inputs, claims broader than their retained evidence, and publication hygiene. Reviewer handling correction: a scratch copy retained the checkout's Git metadata pointer, so a scratch ref update temporarily changed the original HEAD. I restored 6741c554219e and verified a clean working tree and matching manifest bindings; tracked file contents were unchanged.

findings.claim: The published verification scripts can report exit 0 when the verification fails.
findings.evidence: In a private copy, I introduced a unittest import failure and ran the exact section J pipeline. It returned 0 and the published run() recorder printed 'RuntimeError: review injected test failure' followed by 'exit: 0'. Running the same pipeline with bash -o pipefail returned 1. Additional negative controls showed the same problem elsewhere: relock.sh.txt returned 0 after 'requirements.lock.repro ... requirements.lock differ: char 25750, line 309'; install-check.sh.txt returned 0 with uv failures of 42 and an SDK import failure of 127; hash-check.py.txt returned 0 for an all-zero digest while printing 'NO FILE OF THIS RELEASE HAS THIS SHA256'.
findings.failure_scenario: A test regression, mismatching reproduced lock, failed installation, or invalid release hash is supplied to these checks. Their recorded or process-level exit status remains successful, so an exit-code consumer cannot distinguish the wrong result from successful verification.
findings.fix: Capture the unittest status before trimming its output and record that status. Preserve unexpected failures through the relock and installation scripts, explicitly handling expected diagnostic diff exits. Make the hash checker exit nonzero for unmatched digests. Re-run the negative controls and update the published script hashes and byte counts.

findings.claim: The claim that this advisory blocked every head since 22:10Z exceeds the recorded CI evidence.
findings.evidence: The purpose states: 'The required osv-scanner check has failed on the lock for every head since 22:10Z, main's own push runs included, so no pull request could merge.' Line 9 describes reading 'one CI job log', and line 30 explicitly names the other records 'main_push_runs_logs_not_read'. A command checking the returned-outputs file found no gh run view command and none of the reported CI run IDs, job ID, head SHA, or job time interval. Section F supports a local reproduction on base 29458b43, not an exhaustive historical CI assertion. research.md:451 repeats the universal claim.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader treats one reported PR job, two workflow-level failure conclusions, and a local base scan as proof that every intervening head failed for this advisory and that 22:10Z was the first affected check.
findings.fix: Limit the narrative to the reported PR job and independently reproduced base failure. Identify the main workflow conclusions as unverified for cause, and remove the 'every head', 'first', and universal merge-blockage assertions unless corresponding primary CI evidence is retained.

findings.claim: Reading the pinned archive and one main commit does not establish that no fixed upstream lock exists anywhere.
findings.evidence: The receipt concludes 'no upstream lock with litellm 1.93.2 or later exists to adopt'. The published sdk-main.sh.txt:10 fetches only 'refs/heads/main' at depth 1. My independent fetch confirmed main fad63774459171b08f889b12fd3b4d6346168c3e and its litellm 1.93.0 pin; the pinned fcc102a archive also pins 1.93.0. Neither input surveys other published upstream revisions or release refs.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer acts on an exhaustive upstream-availability claim, although the evidence excludes all upstream refs except the inspected main commit and pinned archive.
findings.fix: Replace the assertion with 'the pinned SDK archive and inspected main commit still pin litellm 1.93.0; no fixed lock was found in those inputs'. Retain the named commits and observation time.

findings.claim: The added public evidence exposes private session names and owner aliases.
findings.evidence: The hygiene scan found receipt line 8 publishing 'bc, <previous owner session>', 'session <merge-train owner session>', and 'session <Gate A owner session>'. Line 179 repeats the owner alias. Both added ordinary scanner outputs also retain 'owner: <previous owner>, session <previous owner session>' at lines 52 and 55. These are actual coordination identifiers, unlike the generic path placeholders and path-detection regexes.
findings.failure_scenario: Publishing the receipt and scanner outputs exposes local coordination identifiers in a portable engineering reference.
findings.fix: Replace session names and personal aliases with role descriptions in the receipt and sanitize them in the retained scanner outputs. Keep public issue references and technical evidence, then refresh manifest digests and byte counts.

findings.claim: The recorded observation end precedes completion of the included test run.
findings.evidence: observed_until_utc is '2026-09-30T23:04:45Z'. The returned outputs at line 468 timestamp the start of section J at that same second, and line 470 records 'Ran 233 tests in 12.800s'. The builder header explicitly says command timestamps are start times. Calculating the lower bound gives test completion at 2026-09-30T23:04:57.800Z, after the stated observation end.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader uses observed_until_utc as the end of the receipt's evidence collection, although its included tests had not completed at that time.
findings.fix: Capture the end timestamp after the final command finishes and use it for observed_until_utc. Keep any separate release-window or scanner observation timestamp explicitly scoped to that observation.

findings.claim: The September 28 image scan predates OSV ingestion, not publication of the advisory.
findings.evidence: Line 11 says the '2026-09-28 grype record of that image predates the advisory'. The same receipt at line 64 records NVD publication on 2026-09-02T18:21:28Z. The primary vendor advisory page, fetched on 2026-09-30, says it was published August 26, 2026: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/security/advisories/GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222. The independently fetched OSV record confirms September 30 as its publication time: https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader attributes the image scan's lack of this finding to the advisory not yet existing, although the vendor advisory and NVD record already existed.
findings.fix: Say that the image scan predates the OSV record's September 30 publication. Preserve the limitation that image reachability and a fresh image scan remain unmeasured.

findings.claim: The script claims to query the other upgraded PyPI pins but only queries litellm.
findings.evidence: The docstring promises query results for litellm 'and for the other PyPI pins of the relocked lock that changed in the 2026-09-30 relocks'. Executing 'python3 -B ...osv-advisories.py.txt' produced exactly three query lines, for litellm 1.93.0, 1.93.1, and 1.93.2. The request at lines 27–31 hard-codes package name litellm and has no loop over other packages.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader credits section A with independent package queries for the other upgraded dependencies, although those queries were not performed by this script.
findings.fix: Remove the promise about other PyPI pins from the docstring. The separate full-inventory scanner evidence can remain the evidence for those packages.
